thread.title: Small-Cap Stocks Still Rule; Can The Stock Market Keep Going Up?

author: NANCY GONDO
title: Small-Cap Stocks Still Rule; Can The Stock Market Keep Going Up?
text:
The stock market continued its overall advance the past month, with funds invested in small-cap stocks maintaining their grip on most of the top spots.
X Eight of the top 10 ETFs belonged to the small-cap stocks category based on year-to-date performance through Aug. 14, according to Morningstar Direct. But top honors went to $267.1 million Invesco Russell MidCap Pure Growth ( PXMG ), which tracks the index bearing the same name. The underlying index is composed of stocks from the Russell Midcap Index, which comprises the smallest 800 equities of the Russell 1000 index.
Top holdings in the 97-stock fund as of Aug. 15 included Square ( SQ ), Chipotle Mexican Grill ( CMG ), Paycom Software ( PAYC ), Abiomed ( ABMD ) and O'Reilly Automotive ( ORLY ). Payment processor Square led those stocks with a 108% year-to-date gain, while O'Reilly finished last with a still-solid 35% return.

The other nonsmall-cap is Invesco QQQ Trust ( QQQ ), which tracks the Nasdaq 100 index. The $69.2 billion behemoth is also the biggest ETF in terms of assets. Its top five holdings were Apple ( AAPL ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Microsoft ( MSFT ), Facebook ( FB ) and Alphabet ( GOOG ).
Moving over to sector funds, the top three stayed the same as a month ago: Invesco S&P SmallCap Health Care ( PSCH ), First Trust Dow Jones Internet ( FDN ) and Amplify Online Retail ( IBUY ).
Will The Bull Keep Running? Richard Turnill, BlackRock's global chief investment strategist, expects strong earnings growth to continue driving gains on Wall Street.
"Firms beating expectations have been rewarded with rising stock prices, even as investors fret about rising economic uncertainty, trade frictions and a strong U.S. dollar," he said in a recent report. "Our analysis of corporate guidance suggests company confidence is on the rise — giving us conviction that earnings strength can power on in 2018 amid solid global growth."
